Dear,
Thank you for your interest in graduate studies at the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts School of Music at ASU. As one of the largest universities in the country, the ASU School of Music awards over $2 million to students annually, providing an excellent education at an unbeatable value. ASU's diverse and innovative community is a perfect complement to the personal attention you will receive in the School of Music. With a population of around 750 students, we offer small class sizes, state-of-the-art facilities and one-on-one instruction from world-renowned faculty. We invite you to consider the ASU School of Music for this important step in your music studies. Dr. Kimberly Marshall Professor Organ Kimberly.Marshall@asu.edu The ASU Organ Studio
The ASU Organ Studio offers graduate students opportunities to increase understanding of the development of the organ and its music, while also allowing students to focus on their area of interest. Kimberly Marshall is an expert on medieval and Renaissance organ music. She specializes in Italian music, and the presence of the Italian baroque organ by Domenico Traeri (1742) and provides an ideal vehicle for exploring this style. Unlike other graduate programs in organ, where the main instruments are in multi-purpose halls that must be shared with chamber, choral and orchestral musicians, the Fritts and Traeri organs are located in a space dedicated to organ playing. Every student receives several hours of regularly scheduled practice times in the ASU Organ Hall each week in addition to lessons. Kimberly Marshall is committed to helping each of her graduate students find a unique voice in playing the organ, whether through church work, pedagogy, concert performances, multimedia collaborations or community relations. All of her graduate students obtain church jobs in the local area within the first year of their studies. Kimberly Marshall also coordinates studio trips to visit important organs in the US and abroad. Recent study tour locations include Mexico, France, the Netherlands, and Saxony.
Degrees offered: Master of Music: Performance Master of Music: Performance Pedagogy Doctor of Musical Arts: Performance

Current tuition and fees are reasonable and may be calculated with the ASU Tuition Estimator. Music Scholarships and teaching assistantships are available. Typical assistantships are 25% which amount to 10 hours of work per week and receive:
Tuition remission covering the non-resident portion of tuition 50% reduction in the resident portion of tuition (excluding fees) $7,450 stipend for the academic year, distributed over bi-weekly paychecks
Spoken English Requirement: If your native language is not English you must meet spoken English requirements before you can be considered for a teaching assistantship. You may complete the ASU SPEAK test (minimum score of 55) which is only available on the ASU campus or by attaining a 26 on the speaking portion of the TOEFL. For full details, please visit this website. Application Process
Step 1: Apply to ASU Graduate Admissions and prepare the following:
Official Transcripts: Sealed hardcopy transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate coursework English Proficiency: Applicants from a country whose native language is not English will be required to show proof of English Proficiency by the application deadline
Step 2: Submit the School of Music Application
Contact information for 3 - 4 references Resume Personal Statement Repertoire List Prescreening (doctoral applicants only) Teaching Assistantship Application (optional)
Step 3: Audition
Complete an ad-hoc audition (doctoral or master's) or a recorded audition (master's applicants only) Applicants should contact Dr. Marshall to arrange an ad-hoc audition date and time. All School of Music materials must be received at least one week prior to the ad-hoc audition date.

View Audition Requirements here International Applicants If you are from a country whose native language is not English, you must provide proof of English proficiency:
TOEFL score of at least 550 (PBT) or 80 (iBT) IELTS overall band score of at least 6.5 with no band below 6.0 Pearson Test of English (PTE) score of at least 60
It is strongly recommended to complete and pass the English proficiency exam prior to beginning the application process. Scores will be accepted for exams taken up to two years prior to your first semester. Applications submitted without a passing TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE score will not be considered. We welcome you to contact us via email to MusicAdmissions@asu.edu if you have any additional questions. We also encourage you to refer to the School of Music website, music.asu.edu, as a resource for your admissions questions.
